before.label: Edinburgh speech.zone — Hidden Markov Models for ASR: three introductory parts
before.assignment: Watch the 3 named parts in order (50:55 combined): Part 1 — model, emissions and duration (16:07); Part 2 — state sequences and trellis (18:26); Part 3 — Viterbi and token passing (16:22). V21 sequence: Gaussian emission model and duration topology; hidden state paths and trellis; Viterbi/token passing and Gaussian fitting. All three parts form a coherent argument, 50:55 combined. Use native discrete example first. Gaussian values are likelihood densities, not posterior model probabilities; compare posteriors with priors. Markov state transitions and conditional-independent emissions are separate assumptions. Best path is not the summed likelihood; negative logs convert probability products into additive costs, not a simple reciprocal distance. Rolling scores use limited memory but recovering the path also needs backpointers or another strategy.

before.label: CS 161 (Computer Security) at UC Berkeley — [CS161 FA26] Lecture 18: TLS
before.assignment: Watch only 9:00–10:27, then 11:00–12:15, then 14:20–15:55, then 23:00–25:25, then 33:05–34:55 (8:32 total).
